morphemes.gloss: noun-incorporated initial built from the NI noun maskihkiy 'medicine, herb, plant medicine'. The free-form short i of maskihkiy lengthens to î when the word incorporates: maskihkîw‑ 'of/with medicine'.
NA noun final: 'person, man, human being'. Same final appears in nêhiyawiyiniw 'Cree person' and many other compound nouns.
NI noun: 'medicine, herb' — the underlying noun the headword's initial is built from. Note the free form has short i; in compounds it lengthens to î.

culturalStory.heading: About the Medicine Man
body: maskihkîwiyiniw is the everyday Plains Cree word for a healer — historically a traditional medicine person who carried plant knowledge, ceremony, and the responsibility of caring for the body, mind and spirit of the people. The word is built transparently: maskihkîw‑ 'of/with medicine' (the incorporated form of NI maskihkiy 'herb, medicine') + ‑iyiniw 'person, man'. The same headword now extends naturally to modern doctors and physicians as well — the noun did not need a new coining.

The plaque art tilts that double meaning forward: a clean, modern clinician — scrub cap, surgical mask, glasses — rendered in tidy black line-work with a blue scrub top and a blue surgical mask. The carved English label is the short, plain Medicine Man. The red syllabics carved above the figure spell ᒪᐢᑭᐦᑮᐏᔨᓂᐤ with the long ᑮ (kî) in the fifth-glyph position — the same long î that Trailforks itself uses on the trail's listing (maskihkîwiyiniw - Medicine Man).

Medicine Man the trail is a short, fast, black-diamond singletrack drop in the Hawrelak network on Edmonton's northwest side — 'just what the doctor ordered, a quick downhill through the trees' in the Trailforks description, with bank turns leading into Riverside Traverse. It sits on ᓀᐦᐃᔭᐤ ᐊᐢᑭᕀ Nêhiyaw‑Askiy (Plains Cree territory).

notes: PHYSICAL SIGN OVERRIDES CATALOGUE: The plaque is carved with the long-î form maskihkîwiyiniw / ᒪᐢᑭᐦᑮᐏᔨᓂᐤ (fifth glyph is ᑮ kî, not ᑭ ki). The current catalogue.json has maskihkiwiyiniw / ᒪᐢᑭᐦᑭᐏᔨᓂᐤ — both missing the long-î diacritic. The plaque's long-î form is independently confirmed by Trailforks' own listing for this trail (trailforks.com/trails/maskihkiwiyiniw-medicine-man/, which displays the name as ᒪᐢᑭᐦᑮᐃᐧᔨᓂᐤ - maskihkîwiyiniw - Medicine Man). Coordinator should update catalogue.json creeName 'maskihkiwiyiniw' → 'maskihkîwiyiniw' and creeSyllabics 'ᒪᐢᑭᐦᑭᐏᔨᓂᐤ' → 'ᒪᐢᑭᐦᑮᐏᔨᓂᐤ'.

Trailforks records the syllabics with the bare-w combining form ᐃᐧ rather than the single-syllable ᐏ ('wi'). Both are valid syllabics renderings of the medial '-wi-'; the fragment uses the single ᐏ for visual cleanliness on the page header (matches the kiwapamitin / backbreaker convention).

Trailforks pick: 'ᒪᐢᑭᐦᑮᐃᐧᔨᓂᐤ - maskihkîwiyiniw - Medicine Man' (trailId 377579), Hawrelak network, Northwest Edmonton. High confidence — exact name match including the Cree, contributed by 'kylemath' (the same project user). Trailhead (53.53526, -113.56008).
